summary: A freeCodeCamp tutorial by Beau Carnes showing how to build a JavaScript/Node.js Discord bot entirely in the cloud on Repl.it without installing anything or paying for hosting. It covers creating a Discord bot account, inviting it to a server, coding a ping/pong bot with discord.js, and adding features such as inspirational quotes from zenquotes.io, encouraging replies to sad words, a Repl.it key-value database for user-submitted messages, and a keep-alive web server with Uptime Robot so the bot runs continuously.
one_line: Step-by-step tutorial for building and free cloud-hosting an "Encourage Bot" Discord bot in JavaScript with discord.js, Repl.it and Uptime Robot.
key_facts: The tutorial is titled "JavaScript Discord Bot Tutorial – Code a Discord Bot And Host it for Free" and was published March 8, 2021 by Beau Carnes.
The tutorial uses the discord.js Node library, the Discord API, and the cloud computing platform Repl.it.
To create a Discord bot account, the user goes to the application page, clicks "New Application", goes to the "Bot" tab and clicks "Add Bot", then confirms with "Yes, do it!".
The bot token is described as the bot's password and should not be shared, since it could allow someone to log in to the bot.
Adding the bot to a server requires the account to have "Manage Server" permissions.
The basic bot replies "pong" when a message's content equals "ping", and the token is read from process.env.TOKEN stored in a .env file.
The inspirational quote feature gets quotes from the API at zenquotes.io, triggered by the message "$inspire".
The starter sad words list is ["sad", "depressed", "unhappy", "angry", "miserable"].
The bot's starter encouraging messages are "Cheer up!", "Hang in there.", and "You are a great person / bot!".
User-submitted encouraging messages are stored in the Repl.it database, a key-value store built into every repl.
The commands added for user management are "$new" to add an encouraging message, "$del" with an index to delete one, and "$list" to show all messages.
The "$responding" command takes "true" or "false" to turn the bot's responses to sad words on or off; anything other than "true" is treated as false.
Repl.it's cheapest paid plan is the Hacker Plan, which includes five always-on Repls.
Uptime Robot can be set up to ping the bot's web server every 5 minutes so the bot never enters the sleeping stage.
The keep-alive web server uses express and listens on port 3000, returning "Bot is running!" to visitors.
